title: Italicized Single Letters

illustrates.quote: Ignore font attributes used for letters that mean letters and are shown standing alone, with or without punctuation. Note this change on the Transcriber’s Notes page.

blocks.text: The spelling hint “*i* before *e*, except after *c*” isn't very helpful, because there are many exceptions.
blocks.features: Boxed plain-serif sentence; the three standing-alone letters i, e, and c (each meaning the letter itself, inside the quoted spelling mnemonic) are italicized; the rest is plain roman.

print.notes: Single boxed sentence; no separate heading block.
print.surroundingText: Follows rule 5.3.2 directly; Example 5-2 (same printed page, 5-3) follows immediately, illustrating 5.3.3.
print.printFeatures: Single bordered box, plain serif black text, no color; only i, e, c italicized.

braille.notes: Two lines, margin of 8 literal spaces stripped; no U+2800 blank-cell filler lines occur in this example. No typeform indicator appears on i, e, or c anywhere in the braille — the attribute is dropped entirely, per 5.3.2, leaving plain contracted UEB (independently re-derived from .txt lines 3898-3899, byte-identical to both runs).

resolution: No disagreement: both runs agree on every field. Braille independently re-derived from references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt lines 3898-3899 (margin 8 spaces) and matches byte-for-byte. Print content read from the boxed illustration on PDF p.129 (printed page 5-3).
